correctness.rationale: The two-round EF/first-order normal-form argument gives a necessary-and-sufficient local-profile invariant for all binary-coloured simple graphs. For paths, each pointed type is computed from the vertex, its at most two neighbours, and existence of colour among the remaining non-neighbours. Since the window uses at most three positions, truncating global colour multiplicities at four is exact. Both append transitions are defined, and a completely exhausted 760-state reachability closure yields exactly 70 invariant sets with the exact 2,3,6,10,14,18,10,5,0,2 minimal-length profile counts; thus the certificate is an all-length finite-state proof, not a finite-size enumeration. A distinct direct 32,766-word experiment to length 14 corroborates the same spectrum. Finally any path with the stated extremal profile needs two internal runs of adjacent colour-1 pairs and three runs of colour-0 pairs (each length at least two), hence at least ten vertices; complement gives the second extremal class. Source code and recorded outputs have been executed from included files. No general-graph or rank-greater-than-two statement is asserted.

originality.rationale: Checked the quantitative all-size claim (70 classes, 62 mixed, sharp least-representative 10, two extremizers), not merely the topic. Brown–Hoshino give uncoloured paths; Mwesigye–Truss give m-coloured linearly ordered structures with the different optimal rank-two bound m²+2m=8 at m=2; Weis–Immerman give order+directed-successor word logic. Two closest published records concern directed paths with no colours and one-red ordered words. Other rank-two calculations cover two-coloured directed cycles (48 types) or ordered words (32,530 mixed types), but neither states nor implies the present undirected adjacency-only quotient. Multiple actual research-record searches located no direct or dominating classification. A specialized earlier solution remains a credible priority risk; absence from searches is not proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: An unindexed specialist classification of rank-two logic on unary-labelled undirected paths, or a hidden table computed from general finite-model results, could state or imply the numbers 70, 62 and the sharp bound ten.
A more general theorem on quantifier-rank spectra of graph-labelled word reducts might yield the same numerical quotient as an unpublished corollary; no proof of global novelty is claimed.
Independent mathematical audit has not been performed; reproducibility check is same-session verification only.

value.rationale: A complete rank-two observational quotient for all two-coloured paths is a natural finite-model-theoretic classification, fixing a graph class and the first nontrivial quantifier depth rather than an arbitrary slice. The exact number of 70 theories and the sharp ten-vertex small-model bound identify an effect of colour predicates not captured by the uncoloured four-vertex cutoff, and give a reusable complete finite test basis for rank-two satisfiability over paths. The two exceptional extremal signatures have a structural run-forcing explanation, not simply a black-box count. Value is confined to this precise invariant; the work does not claim a broad complexity breakthrough or higher-depth classification.
